description: Mid reviewer finds pagination cursor bug and provides good reasoning. Solid mid-level performance.

prContext.title: Add candidate list endpoint with cursor pagination
prContext.instructions: Review for API design and correctness.

groundTruth.description: No auth check — any user can list all candidates across all orgs. Missing org_id filter and Clerk JWT verification.
No max limit — client can request limit=999999, effectively loading entire table. Should cap at 100.

Cursor is parsed as integer but used as string in WHERE id > ?1 — SQLite string comparison on UUIDs produces lexicographic ordering, which is not guaranteed to match creation order. Should use created_at + id composite cursor.
SELECT * returns all columns including sensitive data. Should explicitly select only needed fields.

reviewer_comments.what: No auth check — any user can list all candidates.
reviewer_comments.why: Must verify the user belongs to the org and filter by org_id.
A malicious client can request limit=999999 and OOM the worker.
Could leak PII if columns are added later.

rounds.reviewer_summary: Auth and limit are blocking. Column selection is recommended.

implementer_responses.content: Added auth middleware and org_id filter.
implementer_responses.updated_code: pipelineCandidatesRoutes.use('/*', authMiddleware); ... WHERE org_id = ?1 AND id > ?2
SELECT id, name, email, stage_id FROM candidates

verdict.summary: All three issues resolved. Auth, limit, and column selection look correct.

issue_identification.rationale: Found 3 of 4 bugs (auth, limit, SELECT *). Missed cursor ordering issue. Level 3-4.

prioritization.rationale: Auth and limit flagged as blocking. Column selection as suggestion. Good triage. Level 3-4.

revision_evaluation.rationale: Verified all three fixes. Auth middleware pattern is correct. Level 3-4.

reasoning_quality.rationale: Concrete security and performance rationales. Level 3-4.

ai_direction.rationale: Suggested auth middleware, limit cap, explicit columns — all actionable. Level 3-4.
